does_not_prove: This is what GitHub can confirm. It is not a judgement about whether the code is correct.
It cannot show work done outside this repository, or on a branch that was never pushed.
A passing test suite proves the tests that exist passed — not that the right tests exist.
It does not establish who or what authored the change.
SUPPORTED means the platform record matches the narrow scope written next to the claim. It is not a finding that the claim is true in any broader sense.
A successful workflow run shows that run succeeded. It does not show which tests ran, that all tests or all checks passed, or that a change works.
Only this one workflow run was read. Other workflows, check suites and status checks on the same commit were not.
Every observed fact is GitHub reporting on its own run (PLATFORM_REPORTED). Nothing was re-run or independently observed.
Broader security: not checked. A CI conclusion is not a security review.
The record is not signed. Its SHA-256 shows whether the record changed after it was made, not who made it.

provenance.source: trustshell check <run> --claims-file claims.txt, reading api.github.com; served as public/samples/inspect-39619591025/record.json

unknown.what: What the agent was asked to accomplish. The sample is staged claim text; no task was given or recorded.
What the owner permitted. No policy was in force: Inspect reads a finished run, it does not mediate an agent.
Which executor reported. None did: the statements were written by hand for the challenge.
Whether the check workflow succeeded on commit 5d1c5e3f57e1. The line cites a commit the run is not on, so its outcome was not compared.
Whether GitHub still reports the same. The record is what GitHub said at fetchedAt; reading it again is a separate, online capability, not performed here.
Which TrustShell version produced the record. The record does not name it; its card says only "built by trustshell check --claims".
Everything the record's does_not_prove list names. Kept there, not copied here.
Whether any paid or contractual work was delivered. A SUPPORTED run claim does not establish it, and v0 has no payment part.
